# Forward Reads 
error_forward_reads <- 
  learnErrors(filtered_forward_reads, multithread = n_threads)
## 107513044 total bases in 507137 reads from 8 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
# Forward Error Plot 
forward_error_plot <- 
  plotErrors(error_forward_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) + 
  labs(title = "Forward Reads: Error Model")

# Reverse Reads 
error_reverse_reads <- 
  learnErrors(filtered_reverse_reads, multithread = n_threads)
## 103963085 total bases in 507137 reads from 8 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
# Reverse Error Plot 
reverse_error_plot <- 
  plotErrors(error_reverse_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) + 
  labs(title = "Reverse Reads: Error Model")

# Look at the plots together 
forward_error_plot + reverse_error_plot

# Interpretation 1: This project used 16s rRNA seuqencing with MiSeq250, targeting the V5-V6 region using primer sets: P609D 5′-GGMTTAGATACCCBDGTA- 3′ and P699R 5′-GGGTYKCGCTCGTTR- 3’. Based on these information, estimated ASV bp length was estimated using the webtool SILVA testprobe function. The reverse primer target the 1099bp position on E.Coli’s gene, and the forward primer target at position 784. Thus, the anticipated sequenced length with this primer is 315bps, without the primers, the inserts will be 282 bps. During the trimming and turnication, only primer legnths were cut (33bps), and truncation further removed 2bps on the forward end and 15 bps on the reverse tail, thus, a total of 450bps in R1R2 after trimming. The insert size of 282bps indicated there is sufficient overlapped region (60% of total insert) and I can recover the whole insert of 282 bp in merged ASV.

Interpretation 2:

The observed mean/median merge ASV length is 295bps, which is 13 bps longer than our expectation, suggesting that the expected amplicon length based on nominal E. coli primer coordinates may be underestimating the true amplified region or it’s possible that taxon-specific length variation was present here. Or, it can be insufficient trimming of primers, for which I went back to the fastqc rmd and redid the primer serach in filtered reads and found the sequences were clean indeed, with the following statements seen:

[1] “Forward primer remains in 0 % of filtered forward sequences” [1] “Reverse primer remains in 0 % of filtered reverse sequences”

Thus, given the fact that the insert size was estimated in SILVA testprobe, the dataset is suggesting the real insert size is ~295bps.

Interpretation 3:

I suggest trim around 290-300 bp length given the range seen, i will not use fixed bp size as th length variation within a region is expected and can be biologically meaningful. If fix at mean size of 295bps, i would only retain 1% of the dataset, which is not feasible.

# Subset only ASVs that are 295 bps long 
raw_ASV_table_trimmed <- 
  raw_ASV_table[, nchar(colnames(raw_ASV_table)) >= 290 &
                    nchar(colnames(raw_ASV_table)) <= 300]

# Inspect the distribution of sequence lengths of all ASVs in dataset

Chimera removal identified a large proportion of sequence variants (~84%) as bimeric; however, these were low-abundance ASVs. # A little function to identify number seqs

# Make the table to track the seqs 
track <- cbind(sapply(dada_forward, getN),
               sapply(dada_reverse, getN),
               sapply(merged_ASVs, getN),
               rowSums(noChimeras_ASV_table))

# Plot it!
track_counts_df %>%
  pivot_longer(denoisedF:nochim, names_to = "read_type", values_to = "num_reads") %>%
  mutate(read_type = fct_relevel(read_type, "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nochim")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = read_type, y = num_reads, fill = read_type)) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = sample_names), color = "grey") + 
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") + 
  labs(x = "Filtering Step", y = "Number of Sequences") +

ASV richness plot showed that the majority of samples containing between 100 and 150 ASVs, suggesting moderate microbial diversity and consistent denoising performance. A weak positive relationship between sequencing depth and ASV richness was observed. These results suggest the suitability of the dataset for downstream analyses, although appropriate normalization/rarefraction shall be applied to account for variation in sequencing depth.

## [1] "GTCCACGCCGTAAACGATGAGGACCAAGTGTTGGGGGTGAAACCTCAGTGCTGAAGTTAACGCAGTGAGTCCTCCGCCTGGGGAGTATGCACGCAAGTGTGAAACTCAAAGGAATTGACGGGGGCCCGCACAAGCGGTGGAGTATGTGGTTTAATTCGAAGCAACGCGAAGAACCTTACCAGGCCTTGACATGGGATGCGAAGATGCAGAGATGCATCGGAGGTCAACATCCACACAGGTGGTGCATGGTTGTCGTCAGCTCGTGTCGTGAGATGTTGGGTCAAGTCCCG"        
## [2] "GTCCATGCCGTAAACGATGAGTGCTAAGTGTTGGGAGGTTTCCGCCTCTCAGTGCTGCAGCTAACGCATTAAGCACTCCGCCTGGGGAGTACGACCGCAAGGTTGAAACTCAAAGGAATTGACGGGGGCCCGCACAAGCGGTGGAGCATGTGGTTTAATTCGAAGCAACGCGAAGAACCTTACCAGGTCTTGACATCCAGTGCAAACCTAAGAGATTAGGTGTTCCCTTCGGGGACGCTGAGACAGGTGGTGCATGGCTGTCGTCAGCTCGTGTCGTGAGATGTTGGGTTAAGTCCCG"
class(taxa_addSpecies)
## [1] "matrix" "array"
##### Prepare tax table 
# 1. Add the ASV sequences from the rownames to a column 
new_tax_table <- 
  taxa_addSpecies%>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "ASVseqs") 

# Intuition check 
glimpse(new_tax_table)
## Rows: 1,591
## Columns: 8
## $ ASVseqs <chr> "GTCCACGCCGTAAACGATGAGGACCAAGTGTTGGGGGTGAAACCTCAGTGCTGAAGTTAAC…
## $ Kingdom <chr> "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "B…

## $ Class   <chr> "Bacilli", "Bacilli", "Coriobacteriia", "Actinobacteria", "Bac…
## $ Order   <chr> "Erysipelotrichales", "Lactobacillales", "Coriobacteriales", "…
## $ Family  <chr> "Erysipelotrichaceae", "Lactobacillaceae", "Atopobiaceae", "Bi…
## $ Genus   <chr> "Faecalibaculum", NA, "Coriobacteriaceae UCG-002", "Bifidobact…
## $ Species <chr> "rodentium", NA, NA, "pseudolongum", "dorei", NA, NA, "vulgatu…
# IMPORTANT! Let's do our intuition check 
# This is where we ensure we don't mix up the ASV names!
stopifnot(new_tax_table$ASVseqs == rownames(final_ASV_table_withSeqs))

# Now let's add the ASV names 
rownames(new_tax_table) <- rownames(final_ASV_table)
head(new_tax_table)

## ASV_0003         GTCCTAGCCGTAAACGATGGACGCTAGGTGTGGGGCGATGTCGCTCCGTGCCGCAGCTAACGCATTAAGCGTCCCGCCTGGGGAGTACGGCCGCAAGGCTAAAACTCAAAGGAATTGACGGGGGCCCGCACAAGCAGCGGAGCATGTGGCTTAATTCGAAGCAACGCGAAGAACCTTACCAGGGCTTGACATGACGGTGAAGCGGCGGAGACGCCGTGGCCGAAAGGAGCCGCCACAGGTGGTGCATGGCTGTCGTCAGCTCGTGTCGTGAGATGTTGGGTTAAGTCCCG
## ASV_0004 GTCCACGCCGTAAACGGTGGATGCTGGATGTGGGGCCCTTTTTCCGGGTCCTGTGTCGGAGCTAACGCGTTAAGCATCCCGCCTGGGGAGTACGGCCGCAAGGCTAAAACTCAAAGAAATTGACGGGGGCCCGCACAAGCGGCGGAGCATGCGGATTAATTCGATGCAACGCGAAGAACCTTACCTGGGCTTGACATGTGCCGGACGCCCGCGGAGACGCGGGTTCCCTTCGGGGCCGGTTCACAGGTGGTGCATGGTCGTCGTCAGCTCGTGTCGTGAGATGTTGGGTTAAGTCCCG
## ASV_0005      GTCCACACGGTAAACGATGAATACTCGCTGTTTGCGATATACGGCAAGCGGCCAAGCGAAAGCGTTAAGTATTCCACCTGGGGAGTACGCCGGCAACGGTGAAACTCAAAGGAATTGACGGGGGCCCGCACAAGCGGAGGAACATGTGGTTTAATTCGATGATACGCGAGGAACCTTACCCGGGCTTAAATTGCACTCGAATGATCCGGAAACGGTTCAGCTAGCAATAGCGAGTGTGAAGGTGCTGCATGGTTGTCGTCAGCTCGTGCCGTGAGGTGTCGGCTTAAGTGCCA
## ASV_0006 GTCCACGCCGTAAACGATGAATGCTAAGTGTTGGAGGGTTTCCGCCCTTCAGTGCTGCAGCTAACGCAATAAGCATTCCGCCTGGGGAGTACGACCGCAAGGTTGAAACTCAAAGGAATTGACGGGGGCCCGCACAAGCGGTGGAGCATGTGGTTTAATTCGAAGCAACGCGAAGAACCTTACCAGGTCTTGACATCTTTTGACAATCCTAGAGATAGGACTTTCCCTTCGGGGACAAAATGACAGGTGGTGCATGGTTGTCGTCAGCTCGTGTCGTGAGATGTTGGGTTAAGTCCCG
##           Kingdom         Phylum          Class              Order
## ASV_0001 Bacteria      Bacillota        Bacilli Erysipelotrichales
## ASV_0002 Bacteria      Bacillota        Bacilli    Lactobacillales
## ASV_0003 Bacteria Actinomycetota Coriobacteriia   Coriobacteriales
## ASV_0004 Bacteria Actinomycetota Actinobacteria  Bifidobacteriales
## ASV_0005 Bacteria   Bacteroidota    Bacteroidia      Bacteroidales
## ASV_0006 Bacteria      Bacillota        Bacilli    Lactobacillales
##                       Family                     Genus      Species
## ASV_0001 Erysipelotrichaceae            Faecalibaculum    rodentium
## ASV_0002    Lactobacillaceae                      <NA>         <NA>
## ASV_0003        Atopobiaceae Coriobacteriaceae UCG-002         <NA>
## ASV_0004  Bifidobacteriaceae           Bifidobacterium pseudolongum
## ASV_0005      Bacteroidaceae               Bacteroides        dorei
## ASV_0006    Lactobacillaceae         Ligilactobacillus         <NA>
ASV_tax_table <- 
  new_tax_table %>%
  # add rownames from count table for phyloseq handoff
  mutate(ASV = rownames(final_ASV_table)) %>%
  # Reorder the columns
  dplyr::select(Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species, ASV, ASVseqs)

# Assign the rownames, which is required by phyloseq
rownames(ASV_tax_table) <- ASV_tax_table$ASV

# Take a quick look
glimpse(ASV_tax_table)
## Rows: 1,591
## Columns: 9
## $ Kingdom <chr> "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "B…
## $ Phylum  <chr> "Bacillota", "Bacillota", "Actinomycetota", "Actinomycetota", …
## $ Class   <chr> "Bacilli", "Bacilli", "Coriobacteriia", "Actinobacteria", "Bac…
## $ Order   <chr> "Erysipelotrichales", "Lactobacillales", "Coriobacteriales", "…
## $ Family  <chr> "Erysipelotrichaceae", "Lactobacillaceae", "Atopobiaceae", "Bi…
## $ Genus   <chr> "Faecalibaculum", NA, "Coriobacteriaceae UCG-002", "Bifidobact…
## $ Species <chr> "rodentium", NA, NA, "pseudolongum", "dorei", NA, NA, "vulgatu…
## $ ASV     <chr> "ASV_0001", "ASV_0002", "ASV_0003", "ASV_0004", "ASV_0005", "A…
## $ ASVseqs <chr> "GTCCACGCCGTAAACGATGAGGACCAAGTGTTGGGGGTGAAACCTCAGTGCTGAAGTTAAC…
# Intution check
stopifnot(ASV_tax_table$ASV == rownames(ASV_tax_table), 
          rownames(ASV_tax_table) == rownames(ASV_tax_table))

# Write the table 
write.table(ASV_tax_table, 
            file = "/local/workdir/yz3272/BIOMI6300_IronMicrobiotaProject/02_AssignASVs/ASV_taxonomy.tsv", 
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA)
# And save the track_counts_df a R object, which we will merge with metadata information in the next step of the analysis in nalysis/02_Taxonomic_Assignment. 
save(track_counts_df, file = "/local/workdir/yz3272/BIOMI6300_IronMicrobiotaProject/02_AssignASVs/track_read_counts.RData")
metadata_physeq <- read.csv("/local/workdir/yz3272/BIOMI6300_IronMicrobiotaProject/metadata.csv")
# Construct the phyloseq object 
raw_physeq <- phyloseq(otu_table(final_ASV_table, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
                       # The taxonomy table needs to first be converted into a matrix
                       tax_table(as.matrix(ASV_tax_table)), 
                       # Next, add the sample_data
                       metadata_physeq)

# Check the phyloseq object!
raw_physeq

## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 1591 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]

save(raw_physeq, file = "/local/workdir/yz3272/BIOMI6300_IronMicrobiotaProject/02_AssignASVs/raw_physeq.RData")
